whenToUse:
Use an Avatar to show who: the author of a comment, the people on a
project, the account that is signed in. Give it `imageAlt` when the avatar
is the only thing that says who it is. When the name is printed next to
it, leave `imageAlt` out: the avatar is decorative, and the name is read
once.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a product, team or workspace logo.** An Avatar is always round, so
  it reads as a person. Use an image with its own shape.
- **For status through colour.** The avatar's `color` means nothing. Use
  `status` for presence, and print the status where people act on it (an
  assignee picker): a dot is a glance, not the only cue.
- **For a long list of people.** A group shows who at a glance; past a
  handful, show the count or a list of names instead.
- **For an icon in a circle.** Use the icon itself, or an icon-only
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) when it acts.

do.caption: The name is printed, so the avatar has no imageAlt. A screen reader hears “Mary Thompson” once.

dont.caption: imageAlt repeats the printed name: “Mary Thompson, image, Mary Thompson”.

whenToUse:
Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it
belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar.
A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on
carries the meaning in its own name.

Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words
somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or
a name beside it.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a label or category.** Use a
  [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words,
  a badge holds a number.
- **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast.
- **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything
  is, nothing stands out.

do.caption: The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too.

dont.caption: The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”.

whenToUse:
Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the
sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar.
Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into
stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see.
whenNotToUse:
- **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and
  headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise.
- **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on
  purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space.
- **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own
  border, not a Divider beside it.

do.caption: One line between two groups: the break carries meaning.

dont.caption: A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group.

props.name: children

anatomy.name: Key
anatomy.description: One key cap: a glyph or a short word on a bordered chip, its lower edge thicker like a raised key.

anatomy.name: Group

whenToUse:
Use Kbd wherever the page tells someone which key to press: a hint in a
tooltip, a command palette row, a line of help text, a shortcuts sheet.
These are places where people come to learn a shortcut, so the key gets a
cap. A Menu is not: see below.

Match the platform: ⌘ and ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl and Alt elsewhere. Kbd shows
what it is given and does not detect the platform.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a Menu item's shortcut.** Use Menu's `shortcut` string: menus
  show shortcuts as quiet text at the end of the row, the way desktop
  menus do. The menu is for acting, and a cap on every row would pull the
  eye from the labels. A command palette is the exception: it is where
  shortcuts are discovered, so its rows use Kbd.
- **For code or a value someone types.** Use `<code>`: Kbd is a key, not
  text to copy.
- **To bind the key.** Kbd is display only; the page binds the shortcut.

dont.caption: Left in, the glyphs join the name: a screen reader hears “Search ⌘ K”, and ⌘ is read as “place of interest”.

whenToUse:
Use a Tag to label or categorise: a status on a row, the categories of an
item, the filters applied to a list, the people picked in a field. Where a
tag has to pass AA, use `subtle` or `outlined`: solid hue tags keep one
white label across hues, which the warm ones carry under 4.5:1.

Colour carries meaning here, so it is never the only signal: the text says
what the status is.

In a wrapped list of removable tags on touch, keep at least `--space-6`
between rows. The remove button's touch area reaches 10px above and below
a 24px tag, and neighbouring targets would overlap.
whenNotToUse:
- **For an action.** A tag is a label; its only control is remove. Use a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **For a choice the user toggles on and off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) or a
  Checkbox.
- **For a count.** Use a
  [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs).

dont.caption: The same hues solid: the white label falls under 4.5:1.

whenToUse:
Use a Button for an action on the current page: save, submit, open a
dialog, delete. Use one `primary contained` button per view, for the thing
to do next. Everything else steps down to `outlined` or `ghost`, or to
`secondary`.

**Loading** keeps the button's width and focus and blocks it from acting
again, so a double-submit is impossible and a keyboard user is not dropped
back to the top of the page.
whenNotToUse:
- **To navigate.** A link is not a button. Pass `href` and Button renders a
  real `<a>`: it keeps link semantics, opens in a new tab on middle-click,
  and gets the link cursor. A plain Button with an `onClick` that changes
  the page does none of that.
- **For a setting that stays on or off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs), a
  Switch or a Checkbox.
- **For a link inside running text.** Use Link.

do.caption: One primary button: the thing to do next. The rest step down.

dont.caption: Two primary buttons compete for the same click.

do.caption: Show progress with isLoading: the button stays where focus is, and cannot fire twice.

dont.caption: Disabling it to show progress drops keyboard focus and reads as unavailable.

whenToUse:
Use `ToggleGroup` when the toggles answer one question (which view, which
filters) and `ButtonGroup` when a few actions belong together. Give every
button in a group the same variant and appearance, so the pressed one is
the only one that stands out.
whenNotToUse:
- **To switch between panels of content.** Use Tabs: they own the panel
  and its `tabpanel` role.
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Radio group or Checkboxes:
  a toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For unrelated actions.** Lay out separate Buttons with a gap; joining
  them says they belong together.
- **For more than a handful of options.** Use a Select.

do.caption: One look across the group: only the pressed segment stands out.

dont.caption: A different variant per button reads as several states at once.

whenToUse:
Use a toggle for a setting that is on or off and applies immediately:
Bold, Follow, a filter. The label names the setting, and stays the same in
both states.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Checkbox or a Switch: a
  toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For one of many.** Put the toggles in a
  [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttons-buttongroup--docs), or use
  radios or Tabs. A lone toggle is independent: pressing one does not
  release another.
- **For an action.** Something that happens once (Save, Send) is a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

dont.caption: A label that flips to the action reads as “Unfollow, pressed”, which contradicts itself.

whenToUse:
Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting
terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens
until the form is sent.
Write the label so that checked means yes.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a
  light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit.
- **For one choice out of several.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes
  are independent.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

dont.caption: A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out.

Use a colour picker when any colour is a valid answer: a brand colour, a
chart series, a label someone defines. When there is a palette to follow,
offer it as named swatches.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a few fixed colours.** When only a set of colours is allowed (tag
  colours, a theme accent), use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group of swatches or
  a Select: the picker lets anyone type any colour.
- **To show a colour.** Use a swatch and its hex as text.

dont.caption: A palette to follow but no swatches: people match it by eye and land a few steps off.

Use radios to choose one option from a short list, when seeing every

- **For more than about six options, or options that do not fit on

- **For several choices at once.** Use

- **For a single on or off.** Use a

  that applies at once.

like a light switch: dark mode, notifications, auto-save.
whenNotToUse:

- **For more than two options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group or a Select.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar** (Bold, a filter). Use a

whenToUse:
Use an Accordion for several related sections that most readers only
need some of: an FAQ, groups of settings, the parts of a long form. Each
title should say what is inside, so a reader can pick without opening
every item.

Set `headingLevel` to fit the page: under an `h2`, the items are `h3`, the
default.
whenNotToUse:
- **For one section.** Use a
  [Collapse](?path=/docs/components-data-display-collapse--docs): a text
  button that belongs to the content around it.
- **For views of the same thing, one at a time.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs).
- **For content most readers need.** An accordion trades a shorter page for
  an extra click on everything inside it. Show that content.

dont.caption: One item is not a list of sections. Use a Collapse.

Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking
page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days
that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than
refusing the choice after it is made.

Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28
February, not 3 March.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date
  of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs):
  it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted.
- **For a span inside a form.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here.
- **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content.
  Use the [Event Calendar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-event-calendar--docs)

whenToUse:
Use a Card to group content about one thing, so it reads as a unit: a
person, a plan, a setting. Put headings inside at the level the page
needs; the card has none of its own.

A clickable card is one button, and a button may only hold phrasing
content: use spans for its title and text, not headings or paragraphs,
and put no links or buttons inside it. If a card needs its own actions,
leave it plain and put a button in it.

A card that navigates should be a link (`render={<a href />}`), not a
button with a click handler: a link opens in a new tab and shows its
address.

- **For rows of data to compare.** Use a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): columns line
  values up, cards do not.
- **To show and hide content.** Use an

  [Collapse](?path=/docs/components-data-display-collapse--docs).

Everything in a carousel past the first slide is hidden until the reader
goes looking. Use one for content that is fine to miss: featured items,
examples, a gallery. Give it a `label` that names what is in it.

Prefer no `autoPlay`. Motion pulls the eye away from the rest of the page,
and a slide can move on before it has been read.
whenNotToUse:
- **For content everyone must see.** Show it at once: a list, or
  [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) in a grid, show
  more and hide nothing.
- **For items to compare.** Use a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): side by side
  beats one at a time.
- **For steps in a flow.** Use a
  [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it shows how
  many steps there are and where you are.

do.caption: Featured templates: browsing is optional, and missing one costs nothing.

dont.caption: Account notices the reader must act on, four of them hidden in slides most readers never reach.

anatomy.description: Holds the trigger and the panel; sets the text size.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: A medium-weight text button, underlined on hover.

anatomy.description: The text. With openLabel, a second label replaces it while open.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.description: The content, under the trigger. Its height animates open and shut.

whenToUse:
Use a Collapse for one aside in running content: billing details under a
plan, advanced settings under a form. It is a text button, not a bar,
because it belongs to the content around it, and its trigger reads like a
link in a sentence.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a list of sections.** Use an
  [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-data-display-accordion--docs). Its
  items are full-width bars with dividers because they are the page's
  structure.
- **For a short hint about a control.** Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) or a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), which do not
  push the page down.
- **For content most readers need.** Hiding it costs everyone a click.
  Show it.

do.caption: One aside, under the text it belongs to. The label says what opening it does.

dont.caption: A stack of Collapses is a list of sections. Use an Accordion: its items are real headings, framed and divided.

anatomy.description: One per column, named by its header, in table order. Ticked means shown.

anatomy.name: Reset

whenToUse:
Use a Column Chooser on a table with more columns than most people need at
once, typically six or more, where different people read different ones.
whenNotToUse:
- **To switch between whole layouts** (a summary and a detailed set): use
  saved views, so one choice changes several columns at once.
- **To filter rows.** Hiding a column does not hide rows; use filters in
  the table's toolbar.
- **For a table that fits.** If every column fits on the screens it is
  used on, leave them all shown.

do.caption: A few optional columns beside a locked name column.

dont.caption: A chooser for two columns: one is locked, so there is nothing to choose.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` puts the panes side by side with an upright handle; `vertical` stacks them with a flat one.

props.name: defaultSize
props.description: The first pane's starting size in percent, when uncontrolled.

props.name: minSize
props.description: The first pane's smallest size in percent. Home moves the handle here.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: The first pane's largest size in percent. End moves the handle here.

props.name: handleLabel
props.description: The handle's accessible name. Name it after the first pane: "Resize inbox".

anatomy.name: Pane A
anatomy.description: The first pane. Its size is a percentage of the whole, set by the handle; it scrolls when its content is longer.

anatomy.name: Handle
anatomy.description: A 1px `--border` line with a 24px hit area (44px on touch). Hover and drag turn it 2px `--primary`.

anatomy.name: Pane B
anatomy.description: The second pane: the space the first leaves.

whenToUse:
Use Resizable where people need to trade room between two things they
look at together, and the right split depends on the content: a long name
in a list, a wide table in the detail.

Keep `minSize` above zero (the default is 10%), so a pane cannot be
dragged out of sight with its content still in the tab order.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a fixed sidebar beside the page.** Use the App Shell template:
  its Nav Sidebar has a set width and collapses.
- **For a panel that slides over the page.** Use Drawer.
- **For a column of a table.** Use Table's `isResizable`.
- **For layouts that only change with the window.** Use the
  Multi-column layout template: Resizable is for people, not
  breakpoints.

do.caption: Each handle is named after the pane it sizes: “Resize folders”, “Resize inbox”.

dont.caption: Both handles keep the default name, so a screen reader hears “Resize” twice and cannot tell them apart.

props.description: Names the table for assistive tech. Visually hidden unless `showCaption`.

props.name: showCaption
props.description: Shows the caption above the table.

props.name: isSelectable
props.description: Adds a checkbox column, with a header checkbox that selects every row shown.

props.name: hasRowContextMenu
props.description: Also opens a row's `rowActions` on right click or long press, at the pointer. Off by default: the row then loses the browser's own menu (copy a cell's text, open a link in a new tab).

props.name: density
props.description: Row height. `md` is `--row-height` (48px Default, 36px Compact density); `sm` is one `--space-inline` shorter (40, 32).

props.name: hasStickyHeader
props.description: Keeps the header row in view while the table scrolls inside its container, when something limits the container's height.

props.name: isResizable
props.description: A handle at the end of each column header that drags, or arrow-keys, the column wider or narrower (48 to 1200px). The table is then laid out by its header widths (`table-layout: fixed`): columns without a `width` share what is left, and what no longer fits is clipped.

anatomy.name: Caption
anatomy.description: Names the table. Visually hidden unless showCaption.

anatomy.name: Header row
anatomy.description: Small muted labels on --surface-filled. Stays in view with hasStickyHeader.

anatomy.name: Sort button
anatomy.description: The whole header label, with an icon for the sort. Only on sortable columns.

anatomy.name: Select all
anatomy.description: With isSelectable. Selects or clears every row shown, and shows mixed when some are selected.

anatomy.name: Row
anatomy.description: 48px tall (40px at sm), divided by --border. Tinted when hovered or selected.

anatomy.name: Row checkbox
anatomy.description: Named after the row header: "Select Atlas".

anatomy.name: Expand button
anatomy.description: With expandedContent: a ghost icon button. The chevron turns down when open.

anatomy.name: Row header
anatomy.description: The column marked isRowHeader, medium weight: the name a row is known by.

anatomy.name: Row actions
anatomy.description: With rowActions: a ghost "more" button at the end of the row that opens a Menu.

anatomy.name: Expanded row
anatomy.description: One cell spanning every column, under its row, with no rule between them. Holds any layout.

anatomy.name: Total row
anatomy.description: With a footer on any column: a semibold row under a rule, outside the sort.

whenToUse:
Use a Table for records that share their fields, when people compare them
or look one up: projects, invoices, members. Align numbers and dates to the
end, and mark the column a row is known by with `isRowHeader`.

**Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to the
original order, which is often the one that meant something. Uncontrolled,
the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as numbers, text by locale
with "file 2" before "file 10". Empty values sort last both ways.

With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back the
rows already sorted:

**Paging is not built in.** Put a
[Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs) under the
table and pass it one page of `rows`. With `getRowId`, selection keeps
working across pages: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only.
Pass `expandedIds` to open rows from outside the table:
whenNotToUse:
- **For a whole list page** with search, filters, bulk actions and paging.
  Start from the
  [Data Table Page](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs)
  pattern, which puts a Table together with them.
- **For records that do not share fields**, or that are read one at a
  time, like products in a shop. Use [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs).
- **For layout.** A table announces rows and columns to a screen reader;
  use CSS grid to place things side by side.
- **For a spreadsheet**, where arrow keys move between cells and cells
  are edited in place. Table is a plain table, not an ARIA grid; the kit
  has no data grid yet.

dont.caption: Aligned to the start, 9 sits under the 1 of 1,203, and the column cannot be compared at a glance.

do.caption: A row header names each row, so its checkbox reads “Select Atlas”.

dont.caption: Without one, every checkbox is “Select row 1”, “Select row 2”: a screen reader user cannot tell what they select.

whenToUse:
Use a Field round a control that has no label of its own. Keep the helper
text to a line; put a longer rule behind `labelInfo`.
An **error** says what to change, not only that something is wrong.
### Read-only

A value people need to see but cannot change here (set by a rule,
another team or their role) stays a field: put `readOnly` on the control
and say in `helperText` why, and who can change it. Every Zweihänder
control takes `readOnly`. The boxed fields (Text Input, Textarea,
Search, Number Input, Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Date Range Picker)
all look the same: a filled box, still focusable, the value selectable
and submitted with the form. Checkbox, Radio, Switch and Rating keep
their look, since their mark is the value, and only stop changing.

- **Not disabled.** A locked value is still read and copied; a disabled
  one is not (Disabled, below, is for "not yet").
- **No lock icon by default.** The fill already marks the state, and an
  icon would need its own name for screen readers; the helper text says
  more than a lock.
- **A whole record that cannot be edited** is not a form of read-only
  fields: show it as a [Description List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-description-list--docs),
  label and value with no box.
### Disabled

Disable a control only while it does not apply yet, and people can change
that on the same screen: a choice earlier in the form, a step not done.
Say what turns it on, in `helperText` or in the control that does it.

- **Disable for "not yet", hide for "not you", read-only for "not
  changeable here".** An action or a field people's role never lets them
  use, and that they do not need to read, is left out, not shown disabled:
  a control they can never turn on is noise and a support ticket. A value
  they need to see but may not change is read-only.
- **No tooltip for the reason.** A disabled control leaves the tab order,
  so a tooltip on it never opens by keyboard or on touch. Put the reason
  in text people can see; `labelInfo` stays active on a disabled Field.
- **Dimmed on purpose.** Disabled controls are exempt from contrast
  rules and drop below readable contrast, one more reason not to disable
  a value people need to read.
- **Fields that turn off together** go in a disabled
  [`FormFieldGroup`](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs#field-groups):
  every control inside is disabled and dimmed, Checkbox, Switch and Radio
  included, and none is submitted. Slider and File Uploader do not read
  the group: give them `disabled` too.
whenNotToUse:
- **Round a Zweihänder control.** Text Input, Textarea, Number Input,
  Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Checkbox, Switch and Radio have their own
  label, helper text and validation; a Field round one gives it two labels.
- **For a group of controls** under one name, use a
  [`FormFieldGroup`](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs#field-groups)
  (a `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`), or Radio's own group.

- **For a unit people choose** (a currency, a country code). Add-ons take
  text or a `TextInputButton`, not a Select: put a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) beside the field.
- **For a date.** Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).

do.caption: A visible label names the field; the placeholder only hints at the format.

dont.caption: A placeholder as the label disappears on the first keystroke, and with it what the field was for.

do.caption: The error says what is wrong and how to fix it.

dont.caption: A red edge and 'Invalid' leave people guessing what to change.

props.name: max
props.description: The value at which the task is done. The spec calls it `maxValue`.

props.name: size
props.description: Track height: 4px (`sm`), 8px (`md`) or 12px (`lg`).

props.name: isRounded
props.description: Pill ends on the track and the fill.

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour of the fill. `destructive` for a task that is failing or about to run out, such as storage nearly full.

props.name: isIndeterminate
props.description: Progress is happening but how much is unknown: a third of the track slides across.

props.name: showValueLabel
props.description: Shows the percentage after the bar, in tabular figures. Hidden while indeterminate.

props.name: label
props.description: A visible label above the bar; also its accessible name.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Optional, above the bar. Names the progressbar.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: The full length, --secondary.

anatomy.name: Indicator
anatomy.description: The filled share, coloured by variant. A sliding third when indeterminate.

anatomy.name: Value label
anatomy.description: Optional, showValueLabel: the percentage after the bar.

whenToUse:
Use a Progress Bar for a task that takes long enough to wait on and whose
size is known, or will be: an upload, an import, the steps of a setup.
Name the task in the `label`.
`value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage:

Without a visible label, `aria-label` names the bar for screen readers.
Use it only where the context already says what the bar measures.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a short wait with no known size.** Use a
  [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).
- **For content whose shape you know.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout.
- **For steps the user moves through themselves.** Use a
  [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it names the
  steps, and the user can go back.

do.caption: The label names the task, so the reader knows what they are waiting for.

dont.caption: A bare bar leaves sighted readers guessing what it measures, even with an aria-label.

props.name: width
props.description: A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length. Fills the container when omitted; a circle is 40px.

props.name: height
props.description: Of the shape, or of each line with `rows`. A single circle ignores it: its height is its width.

props.name: appearance
props.description: The corners: `square`, `rounded`, or a `circle` for an avatar. With `rows`, a circle draws rounded lines.

props.name: rows
props.description: Lines of text: stacked bars 8px apart, the last one at 60%.

props.name: isFullWidth
props.description: Fills the width of its container, whatever `width` says.

props.name: hasAnimation
props.description: A slow pulse. Off by default: a screen of pulsing shapes is noise.

anatomy.name: Shape
anatomy.description: One bone in --muted, sized like what it stands in for: here an avatar.

anatomy.name: Line
anatomy.description: With rows, one line of text.

anatomy.name: Last line
anatomy.description: At 60%, like the end of a paragraph.

whenToUse:
Use a Skeleton when you know the shape of what is loading: a list, a card,
a profile. Match the shapes to the content that will replace them, with
the same sizes and the same gaps.

Animate the few shapes that matter, or none: `hasAnimation` is off by
default because a screen of pulsing shapes is noise.
whenNotToUse:
- **When you do not know the shape of what is coming.** Use a
  [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).
- **For a long task with a known size.** Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).
- **For a load that is usually instant.** A skeleton that flashes for
  200ms is noise; show nothing, or a Spinner with a `delay`.

do.caption: Shapes of the content that is coming: the layout holds when it arrives.

dont.caption: One block for a whole card jumps to a different layout on load, which is worse than a spinner.

props.name: size
props.description: The ring: 16px (`sm`), 24px (`md`) or 32px (`lg`) across.

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour of the indicator. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds before anything shows, so a fast load never flashes a spinner. The live region is there from the start.

props.name: isIndeterminate
props.description: Spin even when `value` is given.

props.name: label
props.description: Shown under the indicator, and its accessible name. Without one the name is "Loading", visually hidden.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: The full ring, --border. Frames the motion; decoration.

anatomy.name: Indicator
anatomy.description: The arc: a quarter turn while spinning, or the value as a share of the ring.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Optional, under the ring. Also the accessible name.

whenToUse:
Use a Spinner when something is loading and you cannot say what its result
will look like or how long it will take. Use one per region that is
loading, labelled with what is coming.

Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner only
appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice.
whenNotToUse:
- **When you know the shape of what is coming.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout and says more.
- **For a long task with a known size**: an upload, an install. Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs), or a
  `value` here when space is tight.
- **Inside a button.** Use the Button's `isLoading`: it keeps the button's
  width and focus and stops a second click.

do.caption: One spinner for the region, named for what is coming.

dont.caption: A spinner per card says the same thing three times, and three screen-reader announcements.

props.name: maxItems
props.description: Collapse the middle beyond this many items (2 or more): the first item, "…", and the last `maxItems - 1`. "…" expands them in place.

props.name: separator
props.description: Drawn between items, hidden from screen readers.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: `body-sm` (`sm`) or `body` (`md`).

anatomy.name: Link
anatomy.description: Each level above the current page. Muted, underlined on hover.

anatomy.name: Separator
anatomy.description: A chevron, or any node. Decorative, hidden from screen readers.

anatomy.name: Ellipsis
anatomy.description: With maxItems: a button standing in for the collapsed middle.

anatomy.name: Current page
anatomy.description: The last item. Text, not a link: foreground colour, medium weight.

rows.property: Gap between items, and around the separator

whenToUse:
Use Breadcrumbs on pages three or more levels deep, under the page title,
so a reader can see where they are and jump back up any number of levels.
It is a secondary aid: the main navigation still has to get people
everywhere.

Keep the trail on one line. When it would wrap, collapse the middle with
`maxItems`; the first level and the nearest ones stay in view.

Write each label as the title of the page it opens, short enough to scan.
The last item is the current page, as text: a link to the page you are on
does nothing useful.
whenNotToUse:
- **For history.** Breadcrumbs shows where a page sits, not how the reader
  got there. For "go back", use a Back link or
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **On a flat site.** One or two levels need no trail; the main
  navigation already says where you are.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper: it shows the steps ahead
  too, and which are done.
- **As the main navigation.** Use a Nav Sidebar or Tabs.

do.caption: Collapse a long trail with maxItems: one line, and the levels that matter most stay visible.

dont.caption: A trail that wraps reads as two rows and pushes the page down.

props.name: hotkey
props.description: The letter that toggles it with ⌘ or Ctrl, anywhere on the page. `false` binds nothing: only one palette on a page should own the key.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: In the empty input.

props.name: inputLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the search input.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when nothing matches.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the dialog.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open on first render, uncontrolled.

props.name: isModal
props.description: While open, traps focus, locks page scroll and makes the rest of the page inert. `false` is for pictures of it.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: A dialog near the top of the screen, over a scrim. Opened by its trigger or ⌘K.

anatomy.name: Search input
anatomy.description: Focused on open. Typing filters every group at once.

anatomy.name: Group label
anatomy.description: Names a group: Recent, Commands, an object type. It names the group for a screen reader too.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: The first match is highlighted, so Enter always does something.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Optional. What kind of thing the item is.

anatomy.name: Shortcut
anatomy.description: Optional. The key that does the same outside the palette, as Kbd caps. Shown, not read.

anatomy.name: Key hints
anatomy.description: The keys that work here. Read once, as the input's description.

whenToUse:
In an app with many pages and actions, as a fast way around for people who
use it every day: jump to a record, run a command, without going through
the navigation. Open it from a search button in the sidebar
(`NavSidebarButton appearance="field"`) and from ⌘K.

Keep the palette a shortcut, not the only way: everything in it must also
be reachable from the navigation or a button on the page.
whenNotToUse:
- **To search inside one list or table.** Use a search field above it,
  which filters what is on the page.
- **To pick a value in a form.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs): it fills a
  field, the palette runs something.
- **For a handful of actions on one object.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) on that object.

do.caption: Group the results, start each command with a verb, and put records under their type. Recent first.

dont.caption: One list of bare nouns: Invoice could mean open one, create one or list them all.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Leaves the browser's own menu in place, for an area with nothing to act on right now.

anatomy.name: Area
anatomy.description: The element that takes the right click or long press: a row, a card, an object. Outlined while its menu is open.

anatomy.name: Popup
anatomy.description: A Menu popup, opened with its corner at the pointer.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: An entry, the same as an action menu's: label, optional icon and shortcut.

anatomy.name: Separator
anatomy.description: A rule before the destructive items.

whenToUse:
Use a Context Menu where people act on many things in place, rows of a
table, files, cards on a board, objects on a canvas, and expect the right
click they know from desktop apps. Put the same actions behind a visible
control too, a row's "more" button or a toolbar: the right click is a
shortcut, not the way in.
whenNotToUse:
- **For the only way to an action.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) from a visible
  button, or Buttons; add a Context Menu with the same items on top.
- **On text people read or copy.** A right click there should keep the
  browser's menu: copy, look up, translate.
- **For a tool's commands by category.** Use a
  [Menubar](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menubar--docs).

do.caption: The right click repeats the row's visible actions menu.

dont.caption: Actions only a right click reaches. Nothing on screen says they exist, and keyboard and touch users may never find them.

props.name: href
props.description: Where it goes. Without one (or with `isDisabled`) it cannot navigate and is no longer a link to assistive tech.

props.name: children
props.description: The link text. Say where it goes ("See pricing"), not "click here".

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button; `secondary` is muted, for footers and meta text.

props.name: underline
props.description: `always` inside running text: colour alone does not mark a link. `hover` only where the context already says "these are links", like a nav list.

props.name: isExternal
props.description: Opens in a new tab, with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an external icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Drops `href` and every `on*` handler, so it cannot navigate; sets `aria-disabled`.

anatomy.name: Text
anatomy.description: The link's name, underlined: 1px, 2px on hover.

anatomy.name: External icon
anatomy.description: With isExternal: an arrow out of a box. Decorative; screen readers hear "(opens in a new tab)" instead.

rows.property: Corner radius (the focus ring follows it)

whenToUse:
Use a Link to go somewhere: another page, a section of this one, a file,
an outside site. Inside a sentence, keep the underline; let the link
text say where it goes, so it still makes sense read on its own.

Mark links that leave for another site with `isExternal` only when they
open a new tab, and keep that rare: a new tab breaks the Back button.

With a router, pass its link as `render`. Link merges its class and props
onto it, and the router keeps control of navigation:

```tsx
<Link render={<RouterLink to="/settings" />}>Settings</Link>
```
whenNotToUse:
- **For an action.** Saving, deleting or opening a dialog is a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). A link-styled
  action looks like it will take you away, and does not respond to Space.
- **For a prominent call to action that navigates.** Use a Button with
  `href`: it renders an `<a>` with the weight of a button.
- **For a trail of parent pages.** Use Breadcrumbs.
- **For moving through pages of a list.** Use Pagination.

do.caption: The link text names the destination: it reads on its own, in a screen reader's list of links too.

dont.caption: "Click here" says nothing out of context, and hides where the link goes.

props.name: side
props.description: Which side of the trigger the popup opens on. It flips when there is no room.

props.name: align
props.description: How the popup lines up with the trigger along that side.

props.name: isModal
props.description: While open, locks page scroll and makes the rest of the page inert. `false` leaves the page scrollable and clickable.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: The button that opens it. Menu merges its props onto your element.

anatomy.name: Popup
anatomy.description: The surface: the same as the Select list, at least 12rem wide.

anatomy.name: Group label
anatomy.description: Optional. Names a group of items; muted and small.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: An action, a link or a submenu trigger. One control tier tall.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Optional. Decorative.

anatomy.name: Shortcut
anatomy.description: Optional, display only: it does not bind the key.

anatomy.name: Submenu indicator
anatomy.description: A chevron on an item that opens a submenu.

anatomy.name: Separator
anatomy.description: A rule between groups of items.

anatomy.name: Check
anatomy.description: Shows a checkbox or radio item is on. Its column lines up with the icons.

whenToUse:
Use a Menu for actions that belong to one thing but would crowd the
screen as buttons: the actions on a table row, a card's overflow, a
toolbar's "More". Keep it short, put the most used item first, and give
destructive actions the last place, after a separator.
whenNotToUse:
- **To pick a value for a form.** Use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs) when the list
  is long enough to search.
- **For one or two actions.** Show them as
  [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): a hidden action
  is one fewer person finds.
- **For the app's main navigation.** Use a
  [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) or
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs), which show where
  the reader is.
- **For content: a form, a preview.** Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). A menu holds
  only menu items.

do.caption: Delete last, after a separator, in the danger colour.

dont.caption: Delete between two everyday actions: one arrow key too far and it is chosen.

do.caption: A menu of actions. Each item does something now.

dont.caption: A menu standing in for a form field. Use a Select: it has a label, a value and a form name.

props.name: isModal
props.description: While a flyout is open, locks page scroll and makes the rest of the page inert. `false` leaves the page scrollable and clickable.

anatomy.name: Bar
anatomy.description: The row of menus. One tab stop: the arrows move along it.

anatomy.name: Menu trigger
anatomy.description: A top-level item: File, Edit, View. Highlighted while its flyout is open.

anatomy.name: Flyout
anatomy.description: A Menu popup, with all of Menu's entries.

anatomy.name: Group label
anatomy.description: Optional. Names a group of items.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: An entry, here a checkbox item. Flyouts take every Menu entry: actions, links, submenus, checkbox and radio items.

anatomy.name: Separator
anatomy.description: A rule between groups of items.

whenToUse:
Use a Menubar in a screen that works like a desktop tool, an invoice or
report editor, a spreadsheet, where people look for commands by category
and learn their shortcuts. Name each menu for what it holds and keep the
order people know from desktop apps: File, Edit, View, then your own,
then Help.
whenNotToUse:
- **For the app's navigation.** Use a
  [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) or
  the [Top Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs)'s
  links: they show where the reader is, a menubar does not.
- **For a few actions on one thing.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) from a button, or
  Buttons.
- **To find any command by name.** Add a
  [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-command-palette--docs);
  it can sit alongside the menubar.

do.caption: Commands, grouped by the familiar File, Edit, View, with their shortcuts.

dont.caption: Pages behind flyouts. Navigation belongs in the Nav Sidebar or the Top Bar, where the current page shows.

props.name: totalPages
props.description: How many pages there are. Below 1 counts as 1. Leave it out when `totalItems` is set: the count then comes from `totalItems` and `pageSize`.

props.name: totalItems
props.description: How many rows there are in all. Shows the summary ("21–40 of 340") and, without `totalPages`, sets the page count from `pageSize`.

props.name: defaultPageSize
props.description: Rows per page at first, when Pagination keeps its own state.

props.name: defaultPage
props.description: The page shown first, when Pagination keeps its own state.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: Pages shown either side of the current one.

props.name: boundaryCount
props.description: Pages always shown at each end.

props.name: size
props.description: 24px (`sm`) or 32px (`md`) controls, from the control tiers.

anatomy.name: Summary
anatomy.description: The rows shown out of the total, "21–40 of 340". Only with `totalItems`; announced politely when it changes.

anatomy.name: Previous
anatomy.description: Chevron. Disabled on the first page.

anatomy.name: Page
anatomy.description: A square ghost control with the number, in tabular figures.

anatomy.name: Ellipsis
anatomy.description: "…" where two or more pages are skipped. Decorative.

anatomy.name: Current page
anatomy.description: The only filled control.

anatomy.name: Next
anatomy.description: Chevron. Disabled on the last page.

anatomy.name: Rows per page
anatomy.description: A Select of `pageSizeOptions`. Only when they are passed.

rows.property: Height and minimum width on touch screens

rows.part: Ellipsis, Summary, Rows per page label

whenToUse:
Use Pagination under a long list or table when the reader needs to know
where they are in it and jump to a page: search results, an audit log, an
order history. Put it below the content it pages, and keep the list's
position stable as pages change.

Leave `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` at 1. The control stays short and
keeps the same width as the reader moves, so Next stays under the pointer.

Under a table, pass `totalItems` so the reader knows how much there is.
Offer `pageSizeOptions` only when readers really scan in bulk; three or
four choices (10, 20, 50, 100) are enough.

When the pages have URLs, pass `getHref`, so a page can be opened in a new
tab, bookmarked and shared.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a feed read top to bottom.** Load more as the reader scrolls, or
  with a "Load more" [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs):
  page numbers mean nothing in a stream.
- **For a few items.** If everything fits on one page, show it all.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper.
- **For switching between views of one thing.** Use Tabs.

do.caption: The default range: first, last, and the current page with a neighbour each side, on one line.

dont.caption: Every page number at once wraps over several lines and buries the current page.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` puts each label under its marker; `vertical` stacks the steps, for long descriptions or a narrow column. Bullets are always one row.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `circles` shows every step with its marker and label. `bullets` shows only the current step's label, "Step 2 of 4: Workspace", over a row of dots: for a dialog, a phone, or a flow too long for labels.

props.name: size
props.description: A 32px (`md`) or 24px (`sm`) marker. `sm` takes a 12px label. With bullets the dots stay one size and only the text shrinks.

anatomy.name: Marker
anatomy.description: A disc: a check when complete, the number when current or upcoming, a warning on error.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: The step's name, with its status in hidden text for screen readers.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Optional, small and muted.

anatomy.name: Connector
anatomy.description: The line to the next step: primary once the step is complete.

whenToUse:
Use a Stepper when a task is split into a few steps that must be done in
order, and it helps to know how many are left: checkout, onboarding, an
import wizard. Keep it to three to five steps with a word or two each.
whenNotToUse:
- **For sections the reader can visit in any order.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs).
- **For progress with no steps to name**, such as an upload. Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).
- **For a single-page form.** Headings do the job; a stepper over one page
  promises steps that are not there.

do.caption: Four steps, one word each: the whole flow at a glance.

dont.caption: Ten steps squeeze every label and make the flow look longer than it is. Merge steps, or drop the stepper.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tab selected first, when Tabs keeps its own state.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `underline`: a line under the selected tab, for the sections of a page. `pills`: a filled segment, for switching views in a toolbar.

props.name: size
props.description: 24px (`sm`) or 32px (`md`) tabs, from the control tiers.

props.name: orientation
props.description: A row above the panel, or a column beside it. Arrow keys follow: Left and Right, or Up and Down.

props.name: isFullWidth
props.description: Tabs share the full width equally.

props.name: activateOnFocus
props.description: Select a tab as soon as it gets focus, rather than on Enter or Space. For light panels only.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Keep hidden panels in the DOM, e.g. to preserve a form's state.

anatomy.name: Tab list
anatomy.description: The row (or column) of tabs. With underline, a 1px rule along its edge.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Optional. Decorative, sized to the tab.

anatomy.name: Selected tab
anatomy.description: Medium weight, in the selected colour.

anatomy.name: Indicator
anatomy.description: Marks the selected tab and slides to the next one: a 2px bar (underline) or a lifted chip (pills).

anatomy.name: Tab
anatomy.description: An unselected tab: icon and label, muted until hovered.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.description: The selected tab's content.

rows.property: Corner radius (the focus ring follows it)

whenToUse:
Use Tabs to split one thing into views the reader moves between freely,
in any order: the overview, activity and settings of a project. Every
panel is about the same object, and only one is needed at a time.

Label each tab with a word or two. Labels do not wrap or shrink, so long
ones push the row past its container.

Use `underline` for the sections of a page and `pills` for a view switch
in a toolbar. Name the tab list with `aria-label` when no heading does.
Selection is manual by default: arrow keys move focus, Enter or Space
selects, so a slow panel does not load on every keypress. Turn on
`activateOnFocus` only for light panels.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a sequence.** Steps that must be done in order belong in a
  Stepper.
- **To compare content side by side.** Tabs show one panel at a time; put
  things that are read together on the same view.
- **To go to another page.** Use links, a Nav Sidebar or Breadcrumbs: a tab
  changes the view, not the URL.
- **For one setting with two or three options.** Use a radio group or a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) group:
  that changes a value, not the view.

do.caption: Short labels, a word or two: the row fits, and each reads at a glance.

dont.caption: Long labels run past the edge of the container. Shorten them, or go vertical.

props.name: title

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: Optional, semibold. What happened.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: `children`: what it means and what to do.

anatomy.name: Action

whenToUse:
Use a NavSidebar for an app's main navigation when it has more than five or
so destinations, or will grow: the list runs down and does not wrap. Name
groups by what is in them, keep labels to a word or two, and give every
item an icon if the sidebar can collapse.
whenNotToUse:
- **For three to five sections of one page or object.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs) across the top.
- **For actions.** A sidebar goes places. Put actions in
  [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) or a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs).
- **On a phone, as is.** 16rem is most of a phone's width. In an
  [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) under
  64rem it is always the icon rail, with no collapse button; elsewhere,
  pass `isCollapsed`.
